block_length_sensitivity_analysis.conclusion: Across all block lengths from 3 days to 14 days and full station clustering, PM2.5 MAE improvement remains consistently positive with 95% CIs bounded strictly above zero (e.g. [+0.158, +0.195] for 3d; [+0.159, +0.194] for 7d; [+0.153, +0.201] for 14d; [+0.133, +0.224] for station clusters). Conversely, PM2.5 RMSE improvement spans zero across all block lengths (e.g. [-0.038, +0.098] for 3d; [-0.041, +0.102] for 7d; [-0.046, +0.107] for 14d; [-0.077, +0.147] for station clusters), confirming that RMSE improvement is statistically inconclusive while MAE improvement is robust.

sequence_overlap_audit.statistical_implication: Because consecutive sequences shift by 1 hour, consecutive input feature windows overlap by 23 hours, inducing high autocorrelation in model prediction errors (e_t and e_{t+1}). An unblocked IID bootstrap would artificially underestimate variance by treating auto-correlated residuals as independent. The temporally blocked and station-clustered bootstrap implemented here groups autocorrelated segments into contiguous blocks, preserving intra-block correlation and providing realistic, defensible confidence bounds.
